newsitem.title: USA: US June T-bonds rise to highest level in 2-1/2 wks.
newsitem.headline: US June T-bonds rise to highest level in 2-1/2 wks.

text.p: U.S. June T-bonds rose to their highest level in two-and-a-half weeks in reaction to the jump in U.S. weekly jobless claims, traders said.
"These numbers are forcing people to cover short positions," one futures floor trader said.
Claims increased to 332,000 compared to average trade estimates for a slim decline to 317,000. The prior week's claims number was revised to 324,000, up from original reports of 318,000.
Retail buying, which was light at the opening, turned heavy after the report was released, a floor source said.

June T-bonds initially stalled at 107-27/32, Tuesday's high, but managed to test 107-28/32, the contract's highest level since March 31. June hit 107-28/32 last Wednesday, and failed to re-test that high in reaction to tame U.S. March consumer prices earlier this week.
On Thursday morning, the contract ran into strong trendline resistance at 108-01/32, and some traders said a test of 108-08/32 was unlikely in the near term.
"I don't think 108-08/32 will be tested," one trader said. "Right now, everyone is really long."
Good two-way flows were reported in the pit following U.S. Federal Reserve vice chairwoman Alice Rivlin's comments at the Economic Strategy Institute's trade policy conference.
Rivlin said U.S. economy was "uniformly strong," and said she saw very tight labor markets. Rivlin also said the economy has very high momentum.
June T-bonds back-tracked to 107-23/32, and some floor traders said the contract could slip to 107-18/32 later in the session.
Some said the U.S. February trade numbers, which were released at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT, initially offered mild support.

The overall U.S. trade gap narrowed marginally to $11.59 billion, against average forecasts the U.S. deficit would decline to $10.1 billion, from January's deficit which was downwardly revised to $12.67 billion.
However, traders later said the trade numbers would not lead to downward revisions in estimates for first-quarter Gross Domestic Product (GDP).
They said comments from administration and Federal Reserve officials later in the day may shed more light on the trade numbers. White House economic adviser Janet Yellen speaks at 1230 EDT/1630 GMT.
Federal Reserve governor Laurence Meyer will speak on economic conditions and recent Board initiatives at 1400 EDT/1800 GMT to the Consumer Advisory Council.
And Rivlin will speak again on Thursday. She is scheduled to speak in Philadelphia at the Wharton School's public policy forum at 1630 EDT/2030 GMT after pit trade closes.

At 0845 CDT/1345 GMT, June T-bonds were 09/32 higher at 107-24/32, June 10-year notes were up 05/32 at 105-27/32, September Eurodollars were up 0.025 at 93.73, September T-bills were also up 0.025 at 94.32.
